tasks.title: Split server.js into bounded runtime services
tasks.description: Polaris has strong local coherence, but server.js currently owns config, secrets, WebSockets, agent loops, tool execution, MCP, backlog, evals, Cross-Check, file serving, and orchestration. Split the monolith into bounded modules such as agentRuntime, toolRuntime, sessionStore, contracts, mcpGateway, crossCheck, backlog, and httpRoutes. Keep the desktop-local architecture, but make the WebSocket server an adapter over typed core operations like launchSession, executeTool, transitionTask, recordCrossCheck, and loadMemory.
tasks.plan:
## Overview

server.js is a monolithic module handling config, secrets, WebSockets, agent loops, tool execution, MCP, backlog, evals, Cross-Check, file serving, and orchestration. As features grow, the monolith becomes harder to test, debug, and maintain. This refactoring extracts 8 bounded modules with explicit dependencies and a WebSocket adapter pattern to improve stability and maintainability.

## Architecture

Eight bounded modules will be created:
- contracts.ts: Type definitions and schemas (single source of truth)
- sessionStore.ts: Session state management and persistence
- agentRuntime.ts: Agent spawning and session loops
- toolRuntime.ts: Tool execution and schema validation
- mcpGateway.ts: MCP bridge and tool envelope handling
- crossCheck.ts: Cross-Check approval/rejection logic
- backlog.ts: Task operations and transitions
- httpRoutes.ts: HTTP endpoint routing and file serving

WebSocket server becomes a thin adapter over typed core operations: launchSession, executeTool, transitionTask, recordCrossCheck, loadMemory.

## Key Risks & Mitigations

Risk: Mission-critical code breakage. server.js is the engine of the entire player system.
Mitigation: Incremental extraction with rollback gates. Clear commit boundaries. Smoke tests after each phase.

Risk: Type boundary mismatch. Contracts module must capture all message shapes.
Mitigation: Audit server.js before extraction. Automated schema validation in WebSocket adapter.

Risk: Circular dependencies. Modules may accidentally depend on each other.
Mitigation: Contracts is a leaf. Core services depend only on contracts. WebSocket is a hub.

## Phases

1. Foundation: Extract contracts module
2. Core Services: Extract sessionStore, agentRuntime
3. Core Services: Extract toolRuntime, mcpGateway
4. Core Services: Extract crossCheck, backlog
5. HTTP Routes: Extract httpRoutes
6. WebSocket Adapter: Refactor websocket.ts as thin adapter
7. Integration: Wire modules, test, verify rollback
8. Documentation: Update Architecture.md, JSDoc, topology diagram

## First Proof Unit

Contracts module defined and compiles. All TypeScript types for WebSocket messages, tool contracts, and task orchestration are in src/runtime/contracts.ts and compile without errors.
Proof: npx tsc --noEmit src/runtime/contracts.ts exits with code 0.

tasks.title: Make task orchestration an explicit state machine
tasks.description: The planned LangGraph migration is directionally right, but the first implementation should stay tightly scoped to task lifecycle orchestration. Model planned -> build-started -> cba-complete -> build-finished -> PR-Reviewed-> staged -> production as persisted graph state with formal human gates, proof gates, retry paths, and failure recovery. Use this to replace implicit skill-driven transitions with explicit preconditions, transition rules, and resumable state.
tasks.plan:
## Overview

Task #24 shipped LangGraph stubs (state.py, task_graph.py, task_executor.py). Task #26 makes the state machine authoritative: formal preconditions, real HITL pause/resume, proof gate verification, retry paths, failure recovery, and a sync contract with backlog.json so both existing skills and new LangGraph nodes stay in sync.

## Phases

1. Extend TaskState — add proof_units, proof_results, human_gate_signal, retry_count, error_log, StatusLiteral matching backlog enum
2. Formal Transition Table — transitions.py with preconditions and mutations for each (from, to) pair
3. Real HITL Pause/Resume — executor actually suspends at interrupt nodes; /signal unblocks; stall timeout sets status=stalled
4. Proof Gates and Retry Paths — finish_build_node validates proof units; codex_review retry edge; failed_smoke dead-end node
5. Failure Recovery — @safe_node decorator snapshots state and sets status=failed on exception
6. backlog.json Sync Contract — executor writes status back after each node; /sync-state endpoint in server.js

## First Proof Unit

tasks.title: Create a single source of truth for tool and message contracts
tasks.description: WebSocket types are documented in docs/registries, but runtime handling is still hand-rolled and can drift from the UI, direct tools, and MCP bridge. Move WebSocket messages, direct tool schemas, backlog task schemas, and MCP tool envelopes into JSON Schema or Zod-style contract definitions. Generate docs, validation, and contract tests from the same source so the agent prompt, MCP endpoint, UI handlers, and registries stay synchronized.

tasks.title: Upgrade project memory into ranked retrieval
tasks.description: QueryMemory currently loads Obsidian markdown files and can return all memory at once, which creates prompt bloat and weak relevance control. Add a local retrieval layer with chunking, lexical plus semantic ranking, freshness signals, project and task metadata, cited snippets, and retrieval traces. Default QueryMemory to top relevant excerpts while preserving an escape hatch for full-file reads.

tasks.title: Replace regex-heavy tool safety with capability policies
tasks.description: Polaris already has thoughtful file, shell, installer, worktree, size, and encoding safeguards, but several critical protections depend on command regexes and scattered checks. Introduce normalized capability policy objects that define allowed roots, write modes, network permissions, installer permission, destructive command classes, and per-session trust levels. Make tool execution evaluate these policies before running commands or writes, and emit structured audit events for privileged actions.

tasks.title: Expand agent evals into product-critical acceptance suites
tasks.description: The existing agent eval harness is a strong seed, but it is too small to guard Polaris's behavior as the system grows. Add suites for tool choice, permission refusal, QueryMemory fallback, Cross-Check approval and rejection, backlog transitions, model regressions, latency, token cost, retry behavior, and failure recovery. Report pass rate, tool-call count, token use, latency, and regression deltas in concise scorecards.

tasks.title: Make trust, proof, cost, and recovery visible in the product
tasks.description: Polaris's strongest product idea is an AI command center with trust rails, not just parallel agent sessions. Bring task state, proof state, risk state, Cross-Check state, and cost state into a clearer first-class workflow surface. Add explanations for why a session is waiting, one-click recovery from failed gates, and a guided task lane for plan, build, review, stage, and production promotion.

tasks.title: Add a ship task orchestration capability.
tasks.description: I want to have an orchestration window that monitors all open active sessions for projects and ensures that coordination and conflicts are managed. Reference this file for more information.   docs/orchestrator-design.md
tasks.plan:
## Overview

Add an orchestrator window that auto-activates when two or more sessions are open for the same project. The orchestrator is a passive monitor — it reads session state, detects conflicts, and enables Scott to resolve conflicts and push git/Obsidian updates per session. No commands run from the orchestrator directly.

## Phases

1. Server Foundations: Session registry + 4 new HTTP endpoints (GET /branch-state, POST /reserve-merge-slot, POST /release-merge-slot, POST /dry-run-merge stub). Persist state to orchestrator-state.json in Runtime zone.
2. Git Integration: Worktree state query helper, file contention detection, full dry-run merge implementation (throwaway branch, auto-cleaned).
3. Orchestrator UI Panel: New panel in mockup.html — auto-activates on second session, session cards with branch/worktree/conflict state, push buttons.
4. Conflict Resolution + Merge Serialization: FIFO merge slot queue wired into push flow, Obsidian bridge for session summaries, retry logic, amber conflict alerts.

## First Proof Unit

GET /branch-state returns live session data. curl http://localhost:40000/branch-state returns HTTP 200 with JSON containing featureBranches keyed by branch name with head, worktreePath, and contention fields.

proofUnits.title: /branch-state returns live session data
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: GET /branch-state returns JSON listing all active sessions for the project with branch, worktree path, HEAD SHA, and contention array.
proofUnits.exactCommand: curl -s http://localhost:40000/branch-state | python -m json.tool
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: HTTP 404 — endpoint does not exist.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: HTTP 200 with JSON body containing featureBranches keyed by branch name, each with head, worktreePath, and contention fields.
proofUnits.waiverGuidance: N/A

proofUnits.title: Merge slot queue serializes concurrent requests
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: Two simultaneous POST /reserve-merge-slot requests for the same target branch result in one acquired and one queued with position: 2.
proofUnits.exactCommand: Send two POST /reserve-merge-slot requests with taskNumber 36 and 37, both targeting stage. First should return {status:acquired,position:1}, second {status:queued,position:2}.
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: HTTP 404 — endpoint does not exist.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: First returns {status:acquired,position:1}, second returns {status:queued,position:2}.
proofUnits.waiverGuidance: N/A

proofUnits.title: Dry-run merge detects conflict correctly
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: POST /dry-run-merge with a conflicting source branch returns {status: conflict, conflictFiles: [...]} and leaves the repo clean.
proofUnits.exactCommand: POST http://localhost:40000/dry-run-merge with {sourceBranch:"task/36-orchestrator",targetBranch:"main",cleanup:true}. Then run: git status and git branch to confirm no dry-run-* branch exists.
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: HTTP 404 or stub always returns {status:clean}.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Returns {status:conflict,conflictFiles:[...]} when conflict exists; git status shows clean; no dry-run-* branch exists.
proofUnits.waiverGuidance: N/A

proofUnits.title: File contention detection flags overlapping edits
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: When two active sessions have modified the same file, /branch-state includes that file in the contention[] array.
proofUnits.exactCommand:
1. Open two sessions on same project, both with server.js modified
2. GET http://localhost:40000/branch-state
3. Verify contention array includes server.js
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: contention field missing or always empty.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: /branch-state response has contention: ["server.js"] when both sessions list it as modified.
proofUnits.waiverGuidance: Manual verification with two real sessions is acceptable.

proofUnits.title: Orchestrator panel auto-activates on second session
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: Opening a second agent session for the same project causes the orchestrator panel to appear without manual action; closing back to one session hides it.
proofUnits.exactCommand:
1. Start Polaris (npm start)
2. Open one session for Project A — orchestrator panel should be hidden
3. Open a second session for Project A — orchestrator panel should appear automatically
4. Close one session — panel should hide
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: Panel does not exist or does not auto-activate.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Panel appears on second session open; disappears when count drops to 1.
proofUnits.waiverGuidance: N/A

proofUnits.title: Session cards show correct branch, worktree, and conflict state
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: Each session card displays correct branch, worktree path, HEAD SHA, and file contention indicators sourced live from /branch-state.
proofUnits.exactCommand:
1. Open two sessions on different branches for same project
2. Verify each card shows correct branch and worktree
3. Modify same file in both sessions; verify contention indicator appears
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: Cards show placeholder data or no contention indicator.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Each card matches live git state; contention badge appears on file overlap.
proofUnits.waiverGuidance: N/A

proofUnits.title: Full push flow executes through merge slot
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: Push Git acquires a slot, runs dry-run, executes push if clean, releases slot. A second concurrent push waits in queue until the first completes.
proofUnits.exactCommand:
1. Open two sessions on branches with no conflicts
2. Click Push Git on Session A — verify slot acquired, dry-run clean, push executes, slot released
3. While Session A runs, click Push Git on Session B — verify queued state
4. After Session A completes, verify Session B push runs automatically
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: Push ignores slot coordination or button does nothing.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Pushes complete in order; Session B starts only after Session A slot is released.
proofUnits.waiverGuidance: N/A

proofUnits.title: Amber conflict alert fires on conflict detection
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: When Push Git triggers a conflicting dry-run, an amber alert card appears in the orchestrator panel with conflicting files and diff excerpt. Push is held; git repo stays clean.
proofUnits.exactCommand:
1. Create two branches conflicting on same file
2. Open both as sessions in orchestrator
3. Click Push Git on conflicting session
4. Verify amber alert appears with conflict file list and diff
5. Verify git status shows clean working tree
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: No amber alert; push silently fails or corrupts git state.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Amber alert card shows conflict details; git state clean.
proofUnits.waiverGuidance: N/A

proofUnits.title: Push Obsidian writes session summary to Build Plan
proofUnits.expectedBehavior: Clicking Push Obsidian appends a timestamped session summary (branch, worktree, modified files, conflict status) to the project 3-Build_Plan.md in Obsidian.
proofUnits.exactCommand:
1. Open a session with some modified files
2. Click Push Obsidian in the orchestrator panel
3. Open G:\My Drive\Aesop Academy\Obsidian\Polaris_Build\3-Build_Plan.md
4. Verify a new timestamped session summary block was appended
proofUnits.expectedInitialFailure: Button does nothing; file unchanged; or write fails silently.
proofUnits.expectedPassingEvidence: Build Plan shows new summary block matching the session actual branch/worktree/file state.
proofUnits.waiverGuidance: N/A
